skills.name: Conditional Instruction Following
skills.description: When the user provides explicit conditions, fallback logic, or sequenced prerequisites ("do X first, then Y"; "only if Z is not available"; "proceed only if refund goes to gift card"), the agent fails to respect the conditional structure and either skips a required step, applies the wrong branch, or executes immediately without checking the condition. This differs from simple misunderstanding because the condition is stated clearly and the agent demonstrates awareness of it.
skills.reasoning: A7 requires upgrading basic economy to economy before cancellation but the agent refused; R1 says 'if keyboard unavailable just exchange thermostat' but agent exchanges both; R59 says 'cancel only if not processed in 5 days' but agent cancels immediately; R57, R80, R60 all involve conditions the agent acknowledges but then fails to enforce correctly.

skills.name: Multi-Action Task Completeness
skills.description: When a task involves multiple distinct sub-actions across multiple entities (e.g., look up several orders, modify all pending t-shirts, cancel two reservations and book one new one), the agent completes only a subset of the required actions or stops after the first successful sub-action, leaving the task partially done. The agent does not iterate through all in-scope items systematically.
skills.reasoning: R4 modifies only one of two pending t-shirt orders; R16 cancels one pending order but misses the second and returns from the wrong delivered order; R28 processes returns from the wrong orders; A41 fetches only the first reservation when 6+ were needed; R33 does not retrieve orders W6111398 and W7043598 that were required.

skills.name: Precise Entity and Variant Selection
skills.description: The agent selects the wrong item variant, flight number, reservation, or order when matching the user's stated preferences to available options. This includes choosing a suboptimal option when the user specified a criterion (e.g., maximum zoom, second cheapest, arriving before 7 AM), fetching the wrong reservation when multiple exist, or using a wrong item ID in an action call.
skills.reasoning: A35 books a direct flight when the user wanted the second cheapest one-stop; R52 confirms 5x zoom instead of 10x when user asked for maximum zoom; A38 checks the wrong reservation for a delayed flight claim; R21 passes item ID 4107812777 to modify but the actual order contained 9791469541; R64 selects a 4K silver action camera instead of the 4K waterproof one the user requested.

skills.name: Payment Method and Refund Compliance
skills.description: The agent applies the wrong payment method for a charge or refund, either ignoring the user's explicit payment preference or violating the domain rule that refunds must go to the original payment instrument. This includes selecting the wrong payment_method_id in tool calls, computing an incorrect refund/charge amount, or confirming a payment to a method the user did not specify or that was not used for the original purchase.
skills.reasoning: R83 attempts a credit card refund but the original payment was a gift card; A17 charges baggage fees to a credit card despite the user explicitly requesting gift card payment; A2 and A27 send certificates with wrong amounts (over-compensate without policy basis); R5 and R1 call exchange with incorrect payment_method_id; R45 communicates $10.11 price difference when the correct amount was $9.89.

skills.name: Multi-Term Arithmetic Accuracy
skills.description: When the task requires computing totals, price differences, refund sums, or savings across multiple items or orders, the agent produces incorrect numerical answers. This manifests as omitting the calculate tool call, skipping line items, applying the wrong formula, or not accounting for all relevant quantities before communicating a final amount to the user.
skills.reasoning: R16 should compute 3131.10 + 4777.75 + 367.38 = 8276.23 for total refunds but never calls calculate and reports a wrong total; R21 computes net price difference incorrectly (states $35.54 instead of $42.02); R28 omits the calculate step for a five-term sum; A12 should calculate 2*(228+372) upgrade cost across two passengers but skips this; R19 communicates $31.49 total savings but the correct value including a second order would be $41.64.

skills.name: Action Scope Boundary Control
skills.description: The agent either takes actions that are broader than what was requested (cancelling an entire order when only one item should be removed, updating the user profile address in addition to the order shipping address) or narrower than required (attempting an exchange API call on a still-pending order that requires a modify call instead). The agent does not correctly match the scope of the available action to the state of the resource being operated on.
skills.reasoning: R34 cancels the entire order when only the office chair should be removed; R59 updates the shipping address after cancelling the same order (cancellation makes address update pointless and contradicts user intent); R74 and R79 call exchange_delivered_order_items on orders that are still pending, which requires modify_pending_order_items instead; R30 misidentifies which item in the order is damaged and exchanges the wrong one.
